children: Singapore’s S&P Global PMI declined to 56.7 in October 2026 from 58.1 in September, marking the softest expansion in the private sector since May.
The slowdown in activity growth was mainly attributed to operational constraints, although demand continued to improve, driven by growing customer bases and successful business development efforts.
Employment increased for the fifth straight month, marking the longest streak since 2024.

Firms raised their purchasing levels at a record pace in response to the sharp rise in new orders, while delivery times deteriorated for a fourth successive month, highlighting international shipping congestion, supply shortages, and labour shortages.
On the price front, input cost inflation eased to an eight-month low as staff costs rose at a softer pace.
As a result, selling prices rose more slowly.
Finally, sentiment improved to its third-highest level since data collection began in August 2012, amid optimism about sales and activity growth.

title: Singapore Private Sector Growth at 5-Month Low
